headline: On last trading day, Sensex and Nifty crashed amid heavy FII selling and global risks

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 5 October.

why: Heavy selling by Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) pulling out ₹35,860 crore in September
Concerns over global rate hikes and rising oil prices sparking outflows
Global risks and weak sentiment in international markets
Longest weekly losing run in 25 years for benchmark shares
whatHappening: Sensex crashed 1,000 points and Nifty 50 slipped below 22,300 in the last session
Indian benchmark shares recorded their worst month since March
The market was closed on October 2 for Gandhi Jayanti and remains closed for the weekend
UPI transaction volumes jumped 27% to reach 145 billion in the first half
summary: The Indian stock market extended its losing streak to eight consecutive weeks, marking its worst performance in 25 years. Massive selling by foreign investors and global macro pressures led to a significant drop in benchmark indices during the last session. Trading is currently paused for the weekend and will resume on Monday.
